CHAPTER VIII
COMMUNITY PARTICIPATION
Article 38
(1) The community can participate in the implementation of women's protection in the region.
(2) Participation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out by individuals, groups or social community organizations, non-governmental organizations, educational institutions, religious institutions, business entities and mass media.
(3) Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) may take the form of:
a. providing information or reporting to the competent authority if they become aware of acts of violence against women;
b. taking preventive action against violence towards women;
c. conducting skills training for women; and
d. establishing social community institutions that handle the guidance and empowerment of women.
Further provisions regarding community participation as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be regulated by a Regent Regulation.

Article 5
Women victims of acts of violence have the right to obtain protection, information, integrated services, continuous handling up to the rehabilitation stage, and handling in a confidential manner, whether provided by individuals, groups, or institutions, whether governmental or non-governmental.

REGION
REGARDING
PROTECTION
OF WOMEN
CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Regency Region is the Regency Region of Bekasi. 2. Regent is the Regent of Bekasi. 3. Regency Regional Government is the Regent as an element of regional government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region. 4. Regional Secretary is the Regional Secretary of Bekasi Regency. 5. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and Regional House of Representatives in government affairs that are the authority of the region. 6. Woman is a person of female sex starting from infant, adolescent, adult up to elderly, who has been recognized by law. 7. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to women carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination. Protection of Women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the Regional Government, community, and/or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will or has occurred. 8. 9. Discrimination is any restriction, harassment or exclusion that is directly or indirectly based on human differentiation on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, group, class, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs, which results in the reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and fundamental freedoms in life both individual and collective in the political, economic, legal, educational, social, cultural and other aspects of life. 10. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband, wife, or husband, wife and their child, or father and his child, or mother and her child, or blood relatives in a direct line upward or downward up to the third degree. 11. Household is husband, wife, child, people who have family relations due to blood relations, marriage, milk kinship, care, and representation, and/or domestic workers and reside in that household. 12. Victim is a woman who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence and life vulnerability. 13. Violence is any act that results in or can result in misery or suffering either physically, psychologically, sexually, economically and socially as well as discrimination against victims that causes danger to life, body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom. 14. Violence Against Women is any action that results in or may result in misery or suffering either physically, psychologically, sexually, socio-economically and discrimination, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life. 15. Domestic Violence is any act against a person especially women that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically and/or threats of domestic neglect including threats to commit acts of coercion or deprivation of freedom unlawfully within the scope of the household. 16. Physical Violence is any act that results in pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and or causes death. 17. Psychological Violence is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or other psychological suffering to a person. 18. Sexual Violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and or certain other purposes. 19. Women's Rights are a set of rights inherent in a woman or group of people not to experience discrimination, misery or suffering either directly or indirectly committed by state apparatus or by the state or by regional government apparatus or individuals which are natural rights given by God Almighty. 20. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and or knowing that violence against victims will, is or has occurred. 21. Integrated Service is a series of activities to provide protection for witnesses and victims of violence carried out jointly by relevant agencies or institutions as one unit of health rehabilitation, social rehabilitation, return, social reintegration, and legal assistance. 22. Disability is an individual who has physical or mental limitations. 23. Complaint is a series of actions taken by the organizer of the Integrated Service Center to follow up on reports of acts of violence against victims of violence. 24. Health Rehabilitation is the recovery of victims of violence from health disorders they suffer. 25. Social Rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring the psychological condition and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly. 26. Legal Assistance is legal services provided by companions, law enforcement officers which include providing legal consultation, exercising power, representing, accompanying, defending and taking other legal actions for victims of violence. 27. Return is an effort to return victims of violence from the receiving area/area where violence occurred to the area of origin or family. 28. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims of violence with family, community, institutions or other social environments that can provide protection. 29. Regional Technical Implementation Unit for the Protection of Women and Children hereinafter abbreviated as UPTD PPA is an institution established by the Regional Government to provide services to women and children experiencing criminal and civil problems. 30.

Third Part
Rights of Women Victims of Violence

CHAPTER IV
PREVENTION, PROTECTION SERVICES, AND EMPOWERMENT
First Part
Prevention of Violence Against Women

CHAPTER VI
INSTITUTIONAL FRAMEWORK
Article 32
(1) The Regional Government, in its efforts to provide and administer the handling of protection services for women victims of violence, shall establish the UPTD PPA.
(2) The UPTD PPA as referred to in paragraph (1) is under the regional apparatus responsible to the head of the regional apparatus that administers governmental affairs in the field of women's empowerment and child protection.
(3) The UPTD PPA as referred to in paragraph (2) has the following duties:
 a. coordinating and synchronizing the handling of women's protection services in cooperation with related parties;
 b. maintaining and developing networks and referral systems; and
 c. coordinating the preparation and presentation of reports regarding women's protection.
(4) The UPTD PPA as referred to in paragraph (1) is grouped into the following roles:
 a. health;
 b. psychology;
 c. social-education;
 d. law; and
 e. economy.
(5) Further provisions regarding the establishment, main duties and functions, as well as the management of the UPTD PPA as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 12
Domestic Violence as referred to in Article 8 letter d is in the form of:
a. acts that neglect women within the household scope by a person who is obligated to provide livelihood, care or maintenance to such woman;
b. acts that result in economic dependency by means of restricting and/or prohibiting from engaging in decent work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of a person; and
c. acts committed by family members that result in pain, bruises, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, loss of consciousness and/or cause death.

Article 25
(1) Empowerment of women in the field of education as referred to in Article 23 paragraph (2) letter b is implemented by the Regional Apparatus responsible for Education in the form of organizing formal and non-formal education.
(2) Non-formal education as referred to in paragraph (1) aims to improve the capabilities of women.
(3) Non-formal education as referred to in paragraph (2) includes women's empowerment education, skills education and job training.
(4) The organization of formal and non-formal education as referred to in paragraph (1) is implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 28
The Implementation of Women's Empowerment in the field of employment as referred to in Article 23 paragraph (2) letter e is carried out by Regional Apparatus with authority over labor and other related agencies in the form of:
a. women have equal opportunities without discrimination to obtain employment; and
b. employers who employ female workers are obligated to provide protection that includes welfare, safety and health.

Article 33
(1) In order to coordinate and synchronize policies, programs and activities for the protection of women to eliminate all forms of discrimination and acts of violence against women in the Region, the Regent shall establish a task force, forum, working group or other institution.
(2) The membership of the task force, forum, working group or other institution as referred to in paragraph (1) shall consist of relevant Regional Apparatus, community leaders, religious leaders, and universities.
(3) Further provisions regarding the establishment of the task force, forum, working group or other institution as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be regulated by the Regent.

Article 21
Legal services as referred to in Article 16 letter e to assist victims in undergoing the judicial process by:
a. providing legal consultation that includes information regarding victims' rights and the judicial process;
b. accompanying victims at the investigation, prosecution and examination levels in court hearings and assisting victims to comprehensively describe the violence they have experienced; and
c. coordinating with law enforcement officials, volunteer companions and social workers so that the judicial process proceeds as it should.

Fourth Part
Special Rights for the Protection of Women

Article 34
(1) To guarantee synergy, continuity and effectiveness in the implementation of policies, programs and activities for the empowerment and protection of women, the Regional Government conducts monitoring.
(2) The monitoring as referred to in paragraph (1) is intended to determine developments and obstacles in the implementation of policies, programs and activities for the empowerment and protection of women in the Region.
(3) The monitoring as referred to in paragraph (2) is conducted periodically, starting from the planning stage through the implementation of the policies, programs and activities for the empowerment and protection of women for the current year.
(4) The results of the monitoring as referred to in paragraph (3) shall be reported to the Regent periodically.

Article 7
(1) Women have equal opportunities without discrimination to obtain employment.
(2) Equal opportunities as referred to in paragraph (1) are realized through the fulfillment of women's rights to receive equal treatment from the parties employing them.
(3) Parties employing female workers are obligated to provide protection in accordance with the applicable laws and regulations.
(4) The protection that must be provided by parties employing female workers as referred to in paragraph (3) shall be further regulated by a Regent's Regulation.

3.10.rationale: In the original Indonesian text, the regulation explicitly provides economic empowerment measures that amount to economic support. Pasal 26 states that women’s empowerment in the economic field is implemented through: (a) “pemberian keterampilan dan pelatihan kerja” (provision of skills and job training), (b) facilitation of forming/strengthening productive economic business groups, and (c) facilitation of marketing network development. These provisions were also present in the retrieved English candidates (Article 26) and the judge cited them correctly. Therefore the predicted “Yes” aligns with the source text, and the golden “No” appears incorrect for this indicator.

e. providing education regarding women's rights for the community;

4.1.rationale: The original Indonesian policy clearly includes information/education activities as part of primary prevention of violence against women. Pasal 13 ayat (3) explicitly lists prevention actions including: (b) “melakukan sosialisasi mengenai peraturan perundang-undangan yang berkaitan dengan perlindungan hak perempuan korban kekerasan” and (e) “memberikan edukasi mengenai hak-hak perempuan bagi masyarakat.” These exact points were retrieved in the English candidates and cited by the judge. Thus the judge’s “Yes” is supported by the source text, and the golden label “No” appears to be wrong.
